      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Do I need to install an app to add borders to photos on my phone?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "No, you don't need an app. I do this on my phone every day using just the browser. Any modern smartphone browser can run a web-based border editor like AdBorder. I visit the site in Safari on my iPhone or Chrome on my Pixel, upload a photo from the camera roll, apply a border, and download the framed image without installing anything. This avoids storage bloat, permission prompts, and in-app purchases that come with most dedicated photo apps."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Will editing a photo in the browser reduce its quality?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "In my testing, browser-based border tools process the image locally at its original resolution and re-encode it once when exporting. I choose PNG when I need crisp edges for text, logos, and solid-color borders, and JPEG at 90 percent quality when I want most photographic detail with a smaller file size. I've never noticed meaningful quality loss when using the right output format."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Why can't I find the downloaded bordered photo on my phone?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "This tripped me up the first few times too. On iPhone, downloaded files are saved to the Files app in the Downloads folder, not directly to the camera roll. I open Files, tap Downloads, then long-press the image and choose Save to Photos. On Android, downloads land in the Downloads folder or Files by Google under Images, and they show up in the Gallery app after a short refresh."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "What border style works best for Instagram Stories on mobile?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "I use Polaroid-style borders with a thick bottom margin for my Instagram Stories — they're the most popular choice because the extra white space gives me room for text stickers, mentions, and captions without covering the photo itself. I've found gradient borders work well for Reels covers, while thin solid borders remain my safest choice for feed posts."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Why does my bordered photo get cropped when I upload it to Instagram?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "This happens to me occasionally. Instagram crops uploads that fall outside its supported aspect ratios, typically 1:1, 4:5, or 1.91:1 for feed posts. When I add a border on top of a photo, the final image can exceed those ratios and get trimmed. What works for me is matching the target aspect ratio before exporting, or adding the border inside the frame rather than around it so the photo already fits the ratio."
        }
      }
    ]
  }
